subject: Follow-up: ScaleOps integration — request/response schema & auth checklist
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Beth Liu <beth.liu@scaleops.io>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: ScaleOps integration — request/response schema & auth checklist

Hi Beth — great call today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and a set of technical questions so our engineers can scope the POC. Attaching "sample-payloads.json" with example request/response shapes.

High-level ask: ScaleOps wants a low-latency, multi-tenant endpoint that supports: SDK-based integration, service-account auth for server-side requests, routing to a lower-cost model for background jobs, and function/tool calling for structured outputs (invoice parsing + downstream enrichment).

Open items we need from you:
- Which of your flows are single-turn vs multi-turn? (helps decide chat vs completions)
- Do you plan to stream token-by-token to your UI or consume full responses server-side?
- Any hard stop words / sensitive tokens we should enforce at the API layer?
- Embeddings plan: will you store vectors in your own vector DB or want Redwood-managed vectors? TTL/retention requirements?

Technical clarifications we need to confirm from Redwood side (for your engineers):
- SDK auth: we support bearer tokens (long-lived service account keys) + short-lived ephemeral tokens. Which do you need for your CI/CD and sandbox?
- Routing: we can route by policy (latency-first vs cost-first vs region). Do you want per-route overrides?
- Structured output: we recommend function/tool calling for deterministic JSON extraction (we return both the model-generated JSON and a validation status).
- Reranker: we can run an internal reranker over top-K responses with configurable score thresholds. Typical config: embed(query) -> top 50 -> rerank -> top 5. Is that close to your expectation?

Request/response schema & tokenization questions (please confirm):
- Max_tokens: do you want us to enforce a hard token cap per request or allow dynamic truncation based on prompt tokens?
- Stop sequences: will you supply stop tokens, or do you want Redwood to apply a platform-level default?
- Streaming semantics: in streaming mode we emit incremental chunks and a final done event. Do you need partial structured outputs before finalization?

Next steps / proposed cadence:
1) Tech workshop (40m) with your infra engineer Sam + our runtime lead Connor — propose Fri 2027-08-13 10:00 PT.
2) We'll hand you a short POC checklist and a sample SDK repo.
3) After POC: talk SLA/commit and dedicated routing configuration.

Attachments: scaleops-mvp-scope.pdf (business scope), sample-payloads.json (technical examples).

Thanks — looking forward to the workshop.

—
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
[jasmine_liu@redwood.com]

From: Beth Liu <beth.liu@scaleops.io>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Park <sam@scaleops.io>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 17:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up: ScaleOps integration — request/response schema & auth checklist

Jasmine — thanks for the clear notes and the attachments. Quick answers from our side:

- Flow types: invoice ingestion and enrichment will be single-turn (completions style). Customer support assistant will be multi-turn (chat).
- Streaming: for the support assistant we want streaming to the UI (token-by-token). For batch invoice processing we prefer full responses server-side.
- Stop words: we'll supply stop sequences for the support assistant (e.g., "<END_REPLY>") but want Redwood to enforce stripping of any PII tokens we flag.
- Embeddings: we plan to store vectors in our Postgres + PGVector. Retention: 2 years, with occasional reindexing. We may ask Redwood to host reranking in the short-term while we test.

A few follow-ups:
1) Tokenization differences across models — will we see consistent token counts when we switch model variants (e.g., base-cpu vs base-quantized)?
2) For streaming -> if a structured function call triggers midway, can we get partial JSON so the UI can pre-populate fields?
3) Auth: for sandbox we prefer long-lived service keys; for prod we'd like ephemeral tokens via a short-lived service account.

We're available for the tech workshop on Fri 2027-08-13 10:00 PT — Sam will join. Please share the invite.

—Beth
Beth Liu
Head of Integrations | ScaleOps
Beth.Liu@scaleops.io

[Attachment: scaleops-api-spec-v1.pdf]

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Beth Liu <beth.liu@scaleops.io>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: ScaleOps integration — request/response schema & auth checklist

Beth / Jasmine — adding some technical detail from runtime so your engineers have concrete guidance ahead of the Fri workshop. Quick answers inline below.

> Tokenization differences across models — will we see consistent token counts when we switch model variants (e.g., base-cpu vs base-quantized)?
Short answer: tokenization depends on the tokenizer (BPE/byte-level) associated with the model family, not on quantization. If both variants share the same tokenizer, token counts will be consistent. Quantized runtimes affect throughput/latency, not tokenization. We'll include an off-the-shelf tokenizer check in the SDK to pre-calc prompt token usage.

> For streaming -> if a structured function call triggers midway, can we get partial JSON so the UI can pre-populate fields?
We support incremental structured emission in streaming: the runtime emits "partial_function_payload" events and a final "function_complete" event. Caveat: partial payloads are best-effort and may require the UI to handle corrections on finalization. We'll document event shapes in sample-payloads.json.

> Max_tokens enforcement vs dynamic truncation
We recommend enforcing a soft cap that attempts dynamic truncation of the prompt when the total token budget is exceeded, and returning a specific response code when truncation happens (so your caller can decide to retry or surface a warning). If you need strict guarantees, we can enforce a hard cap that rejects the request when prompt + max_tokens > model_limit.

> Stop sequences & streaming semantics
Stop sequences apply both in non-streaming and streaming; in streaming we stop emitting once the sequence is observed, but a small finalization token(s) may still be emitted depending on model internals. We'll expose a boolean flag `strict_stop` in the SDK to control whether the runtime should trim any trailing tokens post-hoc.

> Structured output / function calling
We strongly recommend using function calling for deterministic JSON. SDK will validate the JSON against a provided schema and return (1) the raw model output, (2) the parsed JSON, and (3) a validation report. If validation fails we can optionally run a repair pass.

> Reranker & embeddings flow
Typical pattern we propose: embed(query) -> vector search (your PGVector) -> fetch topK -> call Redwood reranker (lightweight transformer) with the topK bundled context -> return ranked results. We can host the reranker in Redwood short-term to avoid your infra work; later you can self-host.

I can sketch the SDK auth flows in the workshop (service keys, ephemeral token exchange, and audience claims). Also we have a small Node + Python sample repo we'll hand to you.

Connor O'Brien
Runtime Lead | Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com

From: Beth Liu <beth.liu@scaleops.io>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: ScaleOps integration — request/response schema & auth checklist

Perfect, Connor — that answers a lot. Two quick items before the workshop:

1) For the reranker hosting: we'd take Redwood-hosted for 6 weeks, then switch to self-hosted provided latency is < 120ms P95. Can you confirm typical P95 for the reranker in Redwood-hosted mode?
2) On partial structured payloads: we understand best-effort caveat. For the support UI we want pre-population but with a confidence score per field. Is that supported out-of-the-box?

We'll join Fri 08/13 10:00 PT. Sam will send a calendar invite to Jasmine & Connor.

—Beth

Thanks all — confirmed for Fri 2027-08-13 10:00 PT. Calendar invite received. Final quick notes and owners before the workshop:

Action items:
- Redwood (Connor): prepare a 20-minute runtime deep-dive covering tokenizer check, streaming events (partial_function_payload + function_complete), and SDK auth examples. Include sample P95 numbers for reranker (we'll surface realistic P95: ~80–110ms depending on model/size).
- ScaleOps (Sam): share a short list of top-10 support prompts and a sample invoice payload (JSON) so we can prepare targeted examples.
- Redwood (Marissa): share the sample SDK repo + POC checklist and a short onboarding doc.

Attachments re-linked: scaleops-mvp-scope.pdf, sample-payloads.json.

Looking forward to it — we'll keep the workshop focused and come with runnable examples.

—Jasmine
